newsitem.title: GREECE: UPDATED PRESS DIGEST - GREECE - SEPT 13.
newsitem.headline: UPDATED PRESS DIGEST - GREECE - SEPT 13.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek
press:
ELEFTHEROS TYPOS
--ALKO poll shows New Democracy leading PASOK by a small
margin:
PASOK 30.5
Democratic Social Movement 5.3
Political Spring 4.3
Left Coalition 4.1
Communists 4.0
Undecided 13.5
--Greece decides its new prime minister tonight, in
Simitis-Evert debate.
ELEFTHEROTYPIA
--Wells of support for New Democracy running dry. ICAP poll
shows majority of Greek voters define themselves as 'centre' or
'left', one of the main reasons why New Democracy (considered by
the majority to be representative of the 'right') cannot draw
more voters, leaving PASOK with the ability to draw from a
larger share of electorate.
--New Democracy prepares rousing reception for leader Evert in
Thessaloniki.
--Political Spring: Two major parties auctioning off national
issues
--Left Coalition: Tonight's Simitis-Evert TV debate will go
ahead in the absence of real journalism.
--Democratic Social Movement (DHKKI) euphoric about September
TA NEA
--Political Spring's Andonis Samaras says he wants his party to
play the role of watchdog in the new Parliament.
ETHNOS
-- Tonight, couch potatoes vote. Simitis pursues substantial
dialogue on major issues in debate.
KATHIMERINI
--"A show at dialogue": PASOK leader Costas Simitis and his
opposition ND counterpart Miltiades Evert 'face off' in Greece's
first-ever TV debate tonight. Intense behind the scenes
negotiations turn the 'debate' into a joint appearance in which
both will address themselves only to journalists.
--Opinion polls 'undecided'. The flurry of opinion polls in
recent days has shown that only 60 per cent of the electorate
has decided to vote for either of the two major parties. No
party can be considered a certainty for victory since none,
according to the polls, has reached even a third of the vote.
Smaller parties look to garner 20 percent all together.
--Ban on polls being broadcast on radio or television goes into
effect today.
--Wages to see a difficult 1997. Convergence programme
restricts increases to forecast inflation.
--31 merchant vessels take down the Greek flag in first half
1996. Shipping sources say the figure may reach 50 by the end of
the year.
--Albania's first private bank, Tirana Bank-a Bank of Piraeus
subsidiary-opened its doors yesterday.
--Union of insurance companies (EAEE) disciplinary committee to
investigate charges against Intersalonica.
--Macedonia-Thrace Bank reduces interest rates on loans and
deposits.
--Greece to receive first 'symbolic' delivery of natural gas on
Monday.
IMERISIA
--Simitis, Evert teams working feverishly for first TV screen
test.
--Political Spring member, Professor Dimitris Germidis says
hard drachma policy punishing exporters.
--Foreign press sees a PASOK win on September 22, saying
Simitis is best leader for Greece.
EXPRESS
--Increase in construction activity (20 percent in first half
year) and contained prices in sector. Thrace prefecture sees a
60 percent increase in first half 1996.
--Athens Commerce and Industry Chamber (EBEA) believes the
economy has veered off the convergence track and wants political
parties to provide clear decisions and answers.
--Significant presence of foreign investors on Athens Stock
Exchange again yesterday, in third consecutive day of robust
trading.
KERDOS
--Imminent elections put National Tourism Organisation (EOT)
overseas advertising campaign on hold.
--Tonight's Simitis-Evert debate will show who will be premier
on September 23.
NAFTEMBORIKI
--Public deficit defining economic policies. Finance ministry
sources advocate a more aggressive policy for interest rates to
contain the cost of servicing the public debt both for this year
--Deutsche Bank says decision to call September 22 snap
election is positive for the economy.
--Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
